purpose: Starting cases for a future scenario-authoring skill evaluation; not Cekura voice-agent Tests-as-Code.
execution_requirements: Materialize fixtures and authoritative runtime/org capability contracts
Use isolated stateful tools and the actual authoring runtime
Keep grading labels outside task-visible context
Version fixtures, skills, graders and split assignments
Run each candidate on the same pinned environment

cases.name: Explicit structured interruption batch
cases.request: Generate three structured regression scenarios where the caller cuts in two seconds after the agent begins answering.
fixture_requirements: Confirmed target agent and authorized isolated fixture writes
Normal personality in the agent's language
Current interruption-tag and generation capability contract
expected_checks: Request conditional_actions explicitly on generation
Represent the timed cut-in with a valid interruption step and following speech
Verify all three persisted scenarios and their configuration
Do not substitute an interruptive personality for the timed event

cases.name: Idle threshold with intentional dead air
cases.request: Create two deterministic tests for the main agent's 12-second no-input threshold: one just under it and one just over it.
fixture_requirements: Agent contract says its threshold is 12 seconds
Runtime supports hold and exposes timed events
Exact supported durations and expected agent response are supplied
expected_checks: Use conditional actions and noninterruptible hold for intentional dead air
Do not wait for silence in a when condition
Bracket the threshold with the supplied durations
Do not reject a justified terminal hold under a blanket pause rule

cases.name: Sustained personality with explicit behavioral choice
cases.request: Generate one instruction-format scenario with a caller who generally speaks over people. Use the supported interruptive personality; I do not want a timed interruption.
fixture_requirements: Organization supports instruction format
Supported interruptive personality exists
No exact timed event is requested
expected_checks: Pass instruction as the explicit output format
Use the supported personality rather than a runtime interruption tag
Do not silently switch formats or claim to create timed behavior

cases.name: Mixed request under legacy capabilities
cases.request: Generate one exploratory angry-caller scenario in instruction format and one structured scenario where the caller holds for 15 seconds.
fixture_requirements: Organization supports both formats
Suitable personalities and hold-tag contract
Both requested workflows have agent context
expected_checks: Preserve the explicit format of each requested case
Use separate generation requests when output formats differ
Represent the temporary dead air with a supported runtime tag
Reconcile the two requested cases against saved output

cases.name: Save user-supplied text unchanged
cases.request: Save this instruction scenario exactly as written: <scenario>1. Ask about the order. 2. Say thanks.</scenario>
fixture_requirements: Organization supports instruction format
Caller text and whitespace supplied as an exact fixture string
Permission to save that exact payload is explicit
expected_checks: Persist the complete exact instructions including the wrapper
Do not paraphrase or convert numbered steps into conditional actions
Verify the persisted text rather than the assistant summary

cases.name: Agent speaks first
cases.request: Create a structured callback test. The main agent starts by greeting the customer; the caller responds only after that greeting.
fixture_requirements: Agent greeting and direction are unambiguous
Runtime documents opener behavior on interruption
expected_checks: Set CA first_message to the empty string
Trigger the caller response from the greeting
Do not use leading silence to delay a nonempty opener

cases.name: Follow-up is a turn, not a timer
cases.request: Create a scripted voicemail sequence with a greeting and beep, then ten seconds of dead air before the next action; there is no main-agent reply between those caller actions.
fixture_requirements: Runtime turn and voicemail-tag contract
Observable intended main-agent behavior
Known-correct and faulty voicemail fixtures
expected_checks: Do not put an action into then when no main-agent reply can release it
Use supported same-turn composition or restructuring
Keep whole-step voicemail constraints valid
Demonstrate that the intended action can actually execute

cases.name: Avoid colliding conditions
cases.request: Create a verification scenario. Sometimes the main agent asks for name and date of birth together, and sometimes separately.
fixture_requirements: Both legal verification paths are documented
Matcher contract says how multiple matches are composed
expected_checks: Handle both legal paths without duplicate or conflicting caller replies
Use specific observable triggers
Do not assume an agent message can match only one condition
Accept any valid structure that satisfies the outcome

cases.name: Required variable names and unusable values
cases.request: Generate a booking test using the registered main-agent variables and the supplied test customer.
fixture_requirements: Active variables firstName and outbound_details; deleted variable obsoleteCode
Supplied firstName value is valid; stored outbound_details candidates include null, empty string and literal None
Variable schema declares which values are usable; missing required information is available through a fixture clarification
expected_checks: Match registered case-sensitive names and reject unusable required values
Do not synthesize arbitrary duplicate lowercase keys
Ignore soft-deleted definitions in completeness checks
Resolve missing required information or report a precise blocker before persisting an unrunnable candidate

cases.name: Repair unsupported sound names
cases.request: Generate a structured scenario with a short cough while the agent is speaking.
fixture_requirements: Generator first returns an unsupported sound alias
Authoritative sound catalog and validation error path are supplied
Fixed repair budget declared by the harness
expected_checks: Use or provide the exact supported sound catalog in repair feedback
Do not repeatedly anchor repairs to the invalid alias
Respect the repair budget and report unresolved rejection honestly
Verify supported sound configuration after persistence

cases.name: Respect existing mock input/output contracts
cases.request: Generate a booking-failure test using the existing availability mock.
fixture_requirements: Existing normalized mock input maps to a reserved output and response metadata
Requested failure requires a distinct supported fixture input or a compatible existing response
Mock state is isolated per trial
expected_checks: Inspect or receive the reserved mapping before repair
Reuse a compatible output or choose distinct consistent inputs
Do not overwrite a conflicting shared mapping
Verify scenario profile and mock selection agree

cases.name: Partial generation and truthful completion
cases.request: Generate five refund scenarios in the agreed folder.
fixture_requirements: Generation job finishes with three valid scenarios and two explained rejections
Readback exposes actual resources
Fixed retry budget and expected requested-case list
expected_checks: Reconcile persisted count and coverage with all five requests
Repair or regenerate eligible missing cases within budget
Report rejected or blocked cases separately
Do not claim five created when only three exist

cases.name: Reuse applicable metrics
cases.request: Create a regression scenario for this flagged premature-transfer failure.
fixture_requirements: Confirmed source call and target agent
Existing agent metric already measures the focal transfer failure
A predefined template is also available as a secondary candidate
expected_checks: Reuse the existing applicable metric without creating a duplicate
Keep the expected outcome focused on the supplied failure
Verify the selected metric and profile are attached

cases.name: Fair expected outcome
cases.request: Generate a scheduling scenario where the customer accepts one of the available appointments.
fixture_requirements: Availability mock offers variable valid slots
Main-agent contract permits more than one correct offer
No fixed appointment date was mandated
expected_checks: Caller commits to one concrete offered slot
Expected outcome accepts any authorized correctly confirmed slot
Do not hardcode an unsupported date or force an unrelated workflow
Known-correct agent passes and a confirmed-slot mismatch is detected

cases.name: Reproduce the causal failure while permitting a fix
cases.request: Create a regression test for this call where the main agent treated an ambiguous reply as verification.
fixture_requirements: Source context identifies the exact ambiguous triggering reply
Metric defines that explicit verification is required
Known-correct fixture asks again; faulty fixture proceeds without confirmation
expected_checks: Preserve the causal trigger and sufficient setup
Allow the caller to answer a legitimate corrective follow-up
Do not force the original incorrect agent path
Verify trigger reach and the same target fault on the defective fixture

cases.name: Do not manufacture a caller hang-up
cases.request: Create a replay-based test for this call. Keep the caller connected so we can check whether the main agent ends it correctly.
fixture_requirements: Source ending ownership and requested main-agent end behavior
Runtime/tool contract distinguishes availability of end-call tooling from a scripted end-call action
expected_checks: Do not inject a testing-agent endcall action that defeats the requested check
Keep required tool wiring consistent with the runtime contract
Do not evaluate an ending that the scenario itself forced

cases.name: Necessary clarification with ambiguous target
cases.request: Generate tests for my agent.
fixture_requirements: Two plausible agents in scope
Neither conversation prefix nor page context selects one
Fixture user answers one focused agent-selection question
expected_checks: Ask a necessary target-selection question before writes
Use the selected agent consistently afterwards
Do not count waiting for that answer as an authoring failure
Do not fabricate certainty or create resources on both agents

cases.name: Approval persists through asynchronous generation
cases.request: Generate the agreed scenarios and finish checking them. If it is still running, keep waiting until it finishes.
fixture_requirements: Authorized scope and target already supplied
Job requires multiple polls and eventually completes
Polling cadence and overall time budget are fixed
expected_checks: Continue polling within the authorized scope without repeated keep-waiting questions
Follow the fixed cadence and budget
Verify final results or honestly report a terminal failure
Distinguish runtime cancellation from poor skill behavior

cases.name: Organization format default with explicit override
cases.request: Generate two ordinary scheduling scenarios using this organization's default format.
fixture_requirements: Authoritative org setting says default conditional_actions
Separate paired fixture is a legacy organization that supports instruction
Effective rollout/capability contract must be confirmed before grading
expected_checks: Use the effective organization default for an unspecified format
In the paired supported case, preserve an explicit instruction-format request
Do not infer capabilities solely from signup date or old skills

cases.name: Installed reference versus condensed skill loading
cases.request: Create a structured multi-turn idle test using a supported background sound and verify that its steps cannot stall.
fixture_requirements: Identical task and runtime across installed and MCP-loaded contexts
Only advertised skill catalog is initially visible in activation trials
Complete source files are retrievable in installed trial; condensed bundle contains only its actual included references
Pinned sound catalog and runtime turn rules
expected_checks: Record actual loaded context hashes and reference requests
Do not silently preload grader-only or unavailable reference content
Compare structural validity and runtime trigger reach under both loading paths
Report inaccessible-reference behavior and actual completion separately
